_comment: Retrieval eval. The corpus is deliberately adversarial: several passages per topic that are lexically similar but answer different questions, so a retriever cannot score well by topic-matching alone. Queries include paraphrase cases (dense should win) and rare-literal cases (BM25 should win) to justify the hybrid design empirically.

corpus.text: The country will reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 45% below 2005 levels by 2030, and will achieve net zero emissions by 2050.
Renewable energy will account for 70% of national electricity generation by 2030, up from 35% in 2020.
Unabated coal-fired power stations will be retired from the generation fleet no later than 2035.
The total investment required to deliver the mitigation component is estimated at USD 12.6 billion over the period to 2030.
An annual budget allocation of USD 400 million is committed to the adaptation programme for the first three years.
The Government will issue sovereign green bonds and establish a blended finance facility to crowd in private capital.
Coastal protection works will be constructed along 120 km of shoreline to defend communities against sea level rise and storm surge.
A national multi-hazard early warning system will be established to give at-risk communities advance notice of floods, cyclones and drought.
Climate-resilient crop varieties will be distributed to smallholder farmers in drought-prone districts.
A measurement, reporting and verification system will be established to track emissions across all covered sectors.
The national greenhouse gas inventory will be updated annually and progress reported biennially under the enhanced transparency framework.
The Climate Change Act 2023 establishes legally binding five-year carbon budgets and creates a duty on ministers to meet them.
A National Climate Change Council chaired by the Prime Minister will coordinate implementation across ministries.
The country will engage in Article 6.2 cooperative approaches while ensuring that internationally transferred mitigation outcomes are not double counted.
This contribution is submitted in accordance with Article 4 of the Paris Agreement and the decisions of the Conference of the Parties.
Degraded peatlands will be rewetted to halt ongoing carbon losses from drained organic soils, and LULUCF accounting will follow the reference level approach.
A just transition programme will provide retraining and income support to workers displaced from coal-dependent industries.
Gender-responsive budgeting will be applied so that women and youth benefit equitably from climate investments.
Green hydrogen production and grid-scale battery storage will be supported through targeted research and development funding.
Carbon capture, utilisation and storage will be demonstrated at two industrial sites by 2032.
Emissions from road transport will be reduced through electrification of the public bus fleet and expansion of urban rail.
Methane emissions from paddy cultivation and livestock will be addressed through improved water management and feed practices.
Landfill gas capture will be installed at all municipal waste sites serving populations above 100,000.
Forest cover will be increased to 32% of land area through reforestation and protection of existing carbon sinks.
The conditional element of this target is contingent on the provision of international climate finance and technology transfer.
This chapter describes the geography, topography and prevailing climate of the country.
The methodology follows the 2006 IPCC Guidelines as refined in 2019.
Figures may not sum to totals because of rounding, and all monetary values are in constant 2022 prices.
Emissions in the base year 2005 were estimated at 35 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent.
The population was recorded at 22.2 million at the most recent census, with 18% living in urban areas.
Minimum energy performance standards will apply to all new commercial and residential buildings from 2026.
Third-party verification of reported emissions will be mandatory from the second compliance period.
Facilities emitting more than 25,000 tonnes of CO2 equivalent per year must report annually to the national registry.
Fossil fuel subsidies will be phased out by 2027 and the fiscal savings redirected to social protection.
An economy-wide emissions trading scheme will be introduced with an absolute cap declining by 4% annually.
